title: How to Address a Letter to Canada
description: The Canadian address block: addressee, street, then municipality, province and postal code, with the forms for PO boxes, rural routes and general delivery.
keywords: how to address a letter to canada
answer: Write a Canadian address on no more than six lines: the addressee first, then the street address, then the municipality, province or territory, and postal code on the last line. Canada Post sets different second lines for a PO box, rural route and general delivery. For a civic address, extra delivery information goes between the name and street.

ol: **Extra delivery information, if any.** For a civic address, it goes between the name and the street address.
**Last line.** Municipality, province or territory, and postal code.

blocks.p: Canada Post says the address block may not exceed six lines.

rows: Postal box number and station information
Rural route identifier and station information; a civic address for the rural area goes above it
General delivery identifier and station information

blocks.p: In each case the last line is still municipality, province or territory, and postal code.
When an address is written in both languages, Canada Post's guideline is a solid black vertical line at least 0.7 mm thick between the two versions, with about 10 mm of space on either side.

Write your own address in the same form. Mail without a valid return address cannot be sent back; see [return addresses on Canadian letters](/blog/return-address-on-a-canadian-letter). The last line needs a correct postal code: [Canadian postal code format](/blog/canadian-postal-code-format).
